testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which sign shows a driver might be drunk?

options.text: They drive at a steady speed.
They have alcohol stickers on their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stop for no reason.
questions.explanation: Warning signs of an impaired driver include trouble staying in their lane, trouble keeping a steady speed, or stopping without a clear reason.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do?

options.text: You don't need to tell others what you plan to do.
Use turn signals only if another car is next to you.
Don't use a turn signal if your lane change is obvious.
Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: You must always use turn signals to let other drivers know your plans.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Don't back up in a straight line.
Don't fix drift until you are far off course.
Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull forward to reposition the vehicle as needed.
questions.explanation: When backing up with a trailer, pull forward to reposition your vehicle as needed.

questions.question: What is true about speeding?

options.text: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
It gets you to your destination faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a major cause of fatal crashes.
questions.explanation: Speeding causes many fatal crashes. Never drive faster than the posted speed limit and adjust your speed for road conditions.

questions.question: Which is NOT a suspension system defect?
questions.correctAnswerText: Cracked lights.
questions.explanation: Suspension defects include cracked or broken spring hangers, missing or broken spring leaves, and leaking shock absorbers. Get these problems fixed right away.

questions.question: Where is the safety relief valve usually found?
questions.correctAnswerText: In an air tank.
questions.explanation: The safety relief valve in an air brake system is in the tank that gets air first from the compressor.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Stop the front tires from skidding.
Stop the front tires from overheating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles with air brakes have front brake limiting valves to prevent front wheel skidding. Research shows these are not needed, so leave them in the normal position.

questions.question: How should cargo on flatbed trailers be secured?
questions.correctAnswerText: Tied down.
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down to keep it from shifting or falling off.

questions.question: What do move over laws require?

options.text: Trucks to use the left lane.
All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
All vehicles to use the left lane.
All vehicles to move left if a flatbed trailer is in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: All vehicles to leave the lane next to a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with lights on is stopped on the road, move over laws require drivers to leave the lane next to it if possible. If you cannot move safely, slow down and drive carefully.

questions.question: If you don't know the area where you need to back up, what should you do?

options.text: Get out and walk around to learn the area.
Don't use both mirrors because it causes too much distraction.
Watch someone else back up first.
Turn on your high beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out and walk around to learn the area.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. If you don't know the area, get out and walk around to see your path before you start backing up.

questions.question: The ____ shows the driver how much air pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.correctAnswerText: Supply pressure gauge
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge shows the driver the air pressure in the vehicle's air tanks.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Take the vehicle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Downshift.
questions.explanation: Take turns and curves at a safe speed. Always downshift before you enter a curve.

questions.question: Air tank drains:

options.text: Should not be used in cold weather.
Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
Clean the air in the cab.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Air tanks have drains to remove water and compressor oil that build up in the system. Water and oil damage the brakes. Use manual drains every day.

questions.question: Placards should be used:

options.text: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
If there is open space in the truck.
If hazardous materials in the truck weigh more than 200 pounds.
If hazardous materials create an inhalation hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time a vehicle carries hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Place placards on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. Placards identify the type of materials being carried and warn others of the hazards.

questions.question: To make night driving easier, you should:

options.text: Set the instrument panel lights as low as possible while still reading the gauges.
Not take a nap before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the instrument panel lights as low as possible while still reading the gauges.
questions.explanation: Bright interior lights make it hard to see outside at night. Turn off the interior light and dim the instrument lights to the lowest level that lets you read the gauges.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo:
questions.correctAnswerText: Creates an unstable load.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat makes the load unstable. The truck may become top-heavy and the swinging meat can make steering difficult. Be extra careful on sharp curves and highway ramps.

questions.question: Leaking shock absorbers:

options.text: Will prevent the turn signals from working.
Are safe if the vehicle only drives on highways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show a potentially dangerous defect.
questions.explanation: The suspension system keeps the axles in place. Damaged parts like leaking shock absorbers are potentially dangerous defects.

questions.question: When traction is poor, a driver should accelerate slowly:

options.text: Because it is best to always accelerate slowly.
So they stay in control of the vehicle.
So they do not go faster than the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: So they stay in control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Accelerating too quickly on slippery roads makes you lose control. In poor traction, accelerate slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: Overloading cargo can hurt all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: The electrical system.
questions.explanation: Too much cargo hurts steering, braking, and speed control. Notice how your vehicle handles differently with extra weight.

questions.question: When turning quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Turn more than needed to give extra clearance.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: Turn only as much as necessary to clear the object. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: What are escape ramps?

options.text: Ramps to exit the interstate quickly.
Ramps that connect four-lane and two-lane highways.
Ramps used to safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
Ramps that cannot be used by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ramps used to safely stop runaway vehicles on steep hills.
questions.explanation: Escape ramps are built on steep hills to stop runaway vehicles safely. They are filled with loose, soft material and sometimes have an uphill slope.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.correctAnswerText: Spare electrical fuses.
questions.explanation: Required emergency equipment includes at least one fire extinguisher, spare electrical fuses (unless your vehicle has circuit breakers), and warning devices for parked vehicles like reflective triangles.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which braking system?
questions.correctAnswerText: The service brake system.
questions.explanation: The service brake system works when you press the brake pedal while driving. It applies and releases the brakes during normal driving.

questions.question: Mirror adjustment can only be checked properly if:

options.text: The vehicle is on a slight uphill.
The vehicle is on a slight downhill.

questions.correctAnswerText: The trailer is straight.
questions.explanation: When a trailer is attached to a vehicle, you can only check mirror adjustment correctly if the trailer is straight.

questions.question: If brake pads rub against brake drums and create too much heat:

options.text: The brakes will become extra sensitive.
The air compressor will turn on to cool the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may stop working.
questions.explanation: Brakes heat up during use. If they get too hot, they expand and weaken. This is called brake fade and can cause them to stop working completely.

questions.question: Tires with mismatched sizes:

options.text: Can be used only on a front axle.
Can be used only on a trailer's axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be fixed before driving.
questions.explanation: All tires on a vehicle should be the same size. Check that your tires match when inspecting your vehicle.

questions.question: If a load is not secured on a flatbed trailer, the cargo may:

options.text: Shift or fall off the trailer.
Create a glare that blinds other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift or fall off the trailer.
questions.explanation: On flatbed trailers without sides, cargo must be secured to prevent it from moving or falling during transport.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:

options.text: The tires need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose. Check that the nuts are tight if you see rust in this area.

questions.question: When traveling slower than 40 mph, how many seconds of following distance should you maintain for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length?
questions.correctAnswerText: One second.
questions.explanation: At speeds below 40 mph, keep at least one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. Add one more second for higher speeds.

questions.question: During the pre-trip vehicle inspection test:

options.text: You do not have to identify the ABS.
Windshield wipers do not need to be checked.
Shock absorbers only need to be checked on one axle.
The steering box should be checked for leaks.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering box should be checked for leaks.
questions.explanation: During the external vehicle inspection, you must check that the steering box is securely mounted and not leaking.

questions.question: Why must drivers inspect their vehicles?

options.text: It is usually a company policy.
It is usually a local ordinance.
It is a federal and state law.
It adds to the amount of time drivers are paid.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is a federal and state law.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before driving. This ensures the vehicle is safe to operate.

questions.question: When inspecting a power steering system, you should check that:

options.text: The fluid is at the proper level.
The hoses are connected to the battery.
The hoses have no fluid in them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fluid is at the proper level.
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level in the power steering system. Look for leaks and repair them before driving.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding drivers
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of death and injury in work zones. Drive carefully when near road workers.

questions.question: Load securing and vehicle weight laws differ by state. When driving between states:

options.text: The law of the state where the trip started applies.
The law of the state you are in applies.
Request federal regulations to override state laws.
You can choose which state's laws to follow.

questions.correctAnswerText: The law of the state you are in applies.
questions.explanation: Vehicle weight, load securing, load covering, and where large vehicles can drive are regulated by federal, state, and local laws. These vary by location. You must follow the laws of the state you are driving in.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevents the air compressor from overheating
Prevents front brakes from being used on ice
Prevents brake use if downshifting would be more effective

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevents wheel lockup
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops wheels from locking up during hard braking, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in an S-cam brake system, air pressure pushes the rod and moves the:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slack adjuster.
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: If you turn to avoid a hazard:

options.text: Do not brake because it could lock the wheels.
You should turn the wheel very sharply.
You should hold down the brakes until you pass the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not brake because it could lock the wheels.
questions.explanation: Do not apply brakes while turning to avoid a hazard. This can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you would inspect and why.
Estimate the weight of a trailer load.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you would inspect and why.
questions.explanation: On the CDL vehicle inspection test, you must inspect your vehicle and explain to the examiner what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a type of retarder?
questions.correctAnswerText: Air
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow vehicles and reduce brake use. The four types are exhaust, engine, hydraulic, and electric.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
It ensures the vehicle is inspected regularly.
It keeps drivers accountable for inspections.
It provides a plan for the next five trips.

questions.correctAnswerText: It tells the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed.
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the motor carrier about issues that could affect safe vehicle operation or cause breakdowns. Drivers should complete one after each day of driving and note any safety concerns.

questions.question: What can happen if the exhaust system is broken?

options.text: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
Poisonous fumes may exit the back of the muffler.
It may cause problems with a full trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Poisonous fumes may enter the cab.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper berth. Check your exhaust system often for damage.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, slow down by releasing the gas pedal and pushing in the clutch.

questions.question: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Push the brake pedal down.
questions.explanation: To stop a vehicle with air brakes, push the brake pedal down. Pushing harder releases more air pressure and creates a stronger stop.

questions.question: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will:

options.text: Let others see when you brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Still help you steer better.
questions.explanation: If your tractor has ABS but your trailer does not, the ABS will still improve steering control. Watch the trailer and ease off the brakes if it starts to swing.

questions.question: If your trailer has ABS but your tractor does not, can you still drive?

options.text: No. ABS must be on both the tractor and trailer.
Yes, but you should drive slower than usual.
No. You need a new tractor with ABS.
Yes. The tractor and trailer can be used together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes. The tractor and trailer can be used together.
questions.explanation: Having ABS on only the tractor or only the trailer gives you better braking control. You can still drive safely.

questions.question: When carrying cargo, when should you check it?

options.text: Before you start and after the first 50 miles.
Only the loading crew should check it.
Only when you arrive at the end.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start and after the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and then every three hours or 150 miles. You are responsible for keeping cargo secure during the entire trip.

questions.question: Before looking under the hood, you should:

options.text: Set the parking brake and/or place chock blocks.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Set the parking brake and/or place chock blocks.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under the hood, set the parking brake and place chock blocks under the wheels.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of damaged brakes?

options.text: Brake pads with oil or grease on them
Brake pads free of oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: Check for these brake problems: cracked drums, pads with oil or grease on them, and worn or broken pads. Clean pads without oil or grease are normal and safe.

questions.question: Brake fade is caused by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using brakes too much.
questions.explanation: When brakes are used too much, they overheat and become less effective. This is called brake fade.

questions.question: How should you brake if your ABS stops working?

options.text: Push the brake pedal as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake normally.
questions.explanation: ABS is added to your braking system to prevent brakes from locking. If ABS fails, your basic brakes still work. You can drive and brake normally.
